transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Matt (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sara (CTO), Marco (Eng Lead), Jenna (Security PM), Oliver (DevOps)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-packet (security packet), https://docs.redwood.example.com/benchmarks/helix-benchmarks (benchmark spreadsheet)

Summary:
Helix wants a 6-week pilot focused on security posture (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit log fidelity, plus throughput/latency benchmarks to validate cost/latency targets. Primary acceptance criteria include security attestation, successful SSO test, RBAC enforcement, and benchmarked tails under target latencies.

Topics:
- Pilot timeline and acceptance criteria
- Security/compliance gating (SOC 2, ISO27001, encryption, audit logs)
- SSO/SAML and SSO flow testing
- RBAC model and audit log retention/format
- Workload sizing (QPS, token lengths, prompt mix) and benchmark plan
- Private vs Dedicated deployment tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Matt Gonzalez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Matt, AE on this account, and Priya is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Sara Lin: Good, thanks. We have a tight timeline, so hoping to scope the pilot today.
[00:28] Priya Desai: Great. I'll run through the benchmark plan and also the security gating items. Apologies in advance for any background noise, we are on a local cafe WiFi so the auto-transcribe may flub some words.
[00:43] Marco Ruiz: No worries. We're mostly wanting to validate two things: 1) That we can meet a 95th perc latency target for typical user prompts, and 2) That the private deployment satisfies our audit and encryption needs.
[01:05] Jenna Park: And from security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO 27001 cert, SSO via SAML, RBAC mapping to our AD groups, and audit logs with immutable timestamps. Also concerned about key management - we prefer KMS/HSM integration.
[01:28] Matt Gonzalez: Understood. We can provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts — Priya, correct me if I'm wrong on the timing?
[01:36] Priya Desai: Yes, we have our attestation and summary packet ready. We'll share the redacted artefacts — the SOC 2 attestation, ISO cert scan — and an encrypted sitemap of logs. Expect an email from me with links by Monday.
[01:52] Oliver Chen: For connectivity, we need to understand VPC peering vs private on-prem. Helix prefers a VPC flow so traffic doesn't go over public internet. Can Redwood do a private endpoint or dedicated instance in our cloud region?
[02:10] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC-based private control plane and we can also run dedicated GPU pools. There's a small setup window — usually a week for networking and an additional week to provision dedicated capacity if you want reserved GPUs.
[02:29] Marco Ruiz: For benchmarking, our baseline is 200 sustained qps with bursts up to 500 for 1–2 minute spikes. Typical prompt distribution: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (65-512 tokens), 5% long (>512). Cost target is roughly $0.0009 per token average.
[02:51] Priya Desai: Ok, good detail. For the pilot we'll propose a 72-hour steady-state run plus a burst test window. We'll instrument at the request level and token-level to capture p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, and cost estimates. We'll also record KV cache hit rates and prefix caching effects.
[03:11] Sara Lin: Quick question — can Redwood's runtime export audit logs in a format our SIEM ingests? We use Splunk.
[03:20] Matt Gonzalez: We export JSON lines with timestamp, request id, auth principal, resource, and decision metadata. The fields are fairly standard and should map into Splunk. We'll attach a sample export.
[03:36] Jenna Park: How long are logs retained? We need 1 year of immutable audit logs for the pilot for compliance review.
[03:46] Priya Desai: Default retention on hosted is 30 days, but with Private/Dedicated we can configure longer retention or ship logs to your cloud S3 with lifecycle and immutability configured. For the pilot we can set retention to 1 year if you host the archive.
[04:03] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good. Another requirement is SSO. We'll need SAML integration and mapping to AD groups for RBAC. Can you support role-based access and per-route permissions?
[04:17] Priya Desai: Yes. We support SSO via SAML 2.0, and you can map SAML attributes to RBAC roles. Priya: one note the transcribe sometimes renders SAML as 'Sam-el' in earlier notes so just FYI.
[04:34] Oliver Chen: Ha, yeah the auto-transcript is weird. On RBAC — we'd like a three-tier role model: admin, devops, analyst with least privilege. Need to test that during pilot.
[04:47] Matt Gonzalez: We'll provide an RBAC matrix template. For the pilot acceptance we propose: SSO test completed, RBAC exercise with two test users, audit logs flowing to your Splunk instance, SOC 2/ISO artifacts received, and performance benchmarks meeting agreed thresholds.
[05:08] Priya Desai: On the perf thresholds, can we align on specific numbers? We heard 95th perc latency target— is that 150ms for short prompts?
[05:20] Marco Ruiz: That's ideal. For short prompts <=64 tokens we want p95 < 150ms, for medium <=512 tokens p95 < 300ms, and p99 under 1s for medium. Long prompts can be higher but should be predictable.
[05:40] Priya Desai: Ok we can try to hit that on Dedicated with batching tuned. For hosted there may be more variance because of multi-tenancy and batching windows. We can run both in the pilot: a dedicated pool versus hosted baseline and compare.
[05:59] Jenna Park: If we run Private in our VPC, do you support customer-managed KMS? We require keys not held by vendor.
[06:10] Priya Desai: We support KMS integration and HSM connectors for Private deployments. The key IDs are mapped and we never persist plaintext keys. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[06:22] Matt Gonzalez: Great. Now on timeline — Helix asked for a 6-week pilot earlier — let's put a proposed schedule on the table.
[06:32] Priya Desai: Week 1: kickoff, network setup, SSO test account. Week 2: security docs exchange and SAML integration. Week 3: baseline benchmarks on hosted. Week 4: provision dedicated pool and run comparative benchmarks. Week 5: optimization (quantization/kv cache tuning) and security signoffs. Week 6: acceptance and handoff.
[06:58] Marco Ruiz: That seems fine. We might accelerate if we get your SOC 2 docs early. Jenna, you good with that?
[07:07] Jenna Park: Yes, but we want the security packet before we run benchmarks. We'll also want a short threat model review during week 2.
[07:18] Matt Gonzalez: We'll mark that. Priya will send the security packet and also a short checklist for the threat model session.
[07:26] Priya Desai: Another perf note — the runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths and continuous batching; for medium prompts that can reduce tokens/sec cost but may increase tail latency. We'll include toggles in the benchmark scripts so you can see the tradeoffs.
[07:43] Oliver Chen: Regarding metrics, we need exported dashboards for p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit ratio, and model fallback counts.
[07:55] Priya Desai: We will provide dashboard templates and a Grafana link for the test. We'll also provide the raw CSV/JSON output for ingestion.
[08:06] Sara Lin: On data residency — some of our EU customers' data must stay in the EU. Can you deploy the pilot in eu-west-1?
[08:16] Matt Gonzalez: Yes, we have regions in EU and can pin the pilot to eu-west-1 for both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private on-prem we'll need your network details.
[08:27] Jenna Park: A compliance question — do you offer an option for signed, immutable audit logs (WORM)?
[08:33] Priya Desai: We can ship logs to an S3 bucket with Object Lock (WORM) or integrate with third-party immutability services. We'll document the pattern.
[08:45] Marco Ruiz: Metrics for acceptance: 72-hour run with average token cost <= $0.0010 and p95 latencies within agreed bounds for 95% of windows.
[08:58] Priya Desai: We'll instrument sliding windows and provide a pass/fail script to compute those stats.
[09:07] Matt Gonzalez: Let's talk about acceptance criteria example wording so everyone is aligned. I'll read a draft: 1) Receipt of SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation, 2) SSO/SAML integration tested and successful for two AD groups, 3) RBAC mapping validated for admin/devops/analyst, 4) Audit logs exported to Helix Splunk instance and retained for 1 year, 5) Benchmark run (72-hour steady) with p95/p99 within agreed thresholds and cost under target. Any edits?
[09:40] Jenna Park: Add a security review signoff after threat model and include KMS/HSM integration validation.
[09:47] Marco Ruiz: Also add a smoke test for model fallback — if a high-cost model is down, does it fallback gracefully to a cheaper variant with degraded but acceptable latency?
[09:58] Priya Desai: Good call. Redwood supports automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll include the fallback policy and test plan in the benchmark script.
[10:09] Sara Lin: About the benchmark inputs — we'll supply a representative prompt corpus and some real user traces sanitized. Is that ok?
[10:16] Matt Gonzalez: Perfect. We'll need sample traces and a mapping of user types to token lengths. Priya will take that.
[10:24] Priya Desai: For the benchmark script we recommend a steady-state mix generator with spikes and a ramp-up. We'll provide the JMeter-like runner and an example invocation. The runner will create per-request metadata so the audit log includes request mapping.
[10:39] Oliver Chen: For the SAML test — who from Redwood will be the contact to set the IdP config?
[10:44] Matt Gonzalez: Matt and Priya will coordinate. We'll send ACS/Entity IDs and the SP metadata. Priya will be hands-on during the SAML test.
[10:53] Jenna Park: Are there any known limitations with RBAC or attribute mapping we should be aware of?
[10:59] Priya Desai: The main limitation is attribute size and frequency of group sync; large flattened group manifests can be slow, but attribute-based mappings are supported. We'll include best practices.
[11:12] Marco Ruiz: On logging — how are personally identifiable fields redacted in logs? We have strict PII rules.
[11:20] Priya Desai: We provide configurable redaction rules. By default request text is not logged in full; we provide metadata and hashed request identifiers. If you need full request logging for debugging we can do it to a secured S3 with restricted access and time-limited keys.
[11:36] Sara Lin: Ok. For cost, Marco and I want a projected cost model for the pilot and a projection for steady-state at 200 qps — can Redwood share that?
[11:46] Matt Gonzalez: Yes we'll run a cost model. Priya will generate a cost per token projection and an ops-runbook estimate for dedicated GPUs and typical quantization savings.
[11:58] Priya Desai: One more technical diff: our runtime supports continuous KV cache across sessions for conversational workloads; that can reduce tokens/server but has additional privacy considerations. We'll note options to disable persistent caches for the pilot.
[12:16] Jenna Park: We'll probably start with caches off until we validate data handling.
[12:22] Matt Gonzalez: Noted. Now to logistics: we'll propose specific dates for the 72-hour run and send calendar invites after the security packet goes out.
[12:31] Marco Ruiz: On measurement, we want both per-request raw traces and aggregated metrics. Try to keep 1s granularity for tokens/sec and 10s for latency windows.
[12:43] Priya Desai: we'll provide both. Also note the transcribe sometimes merges K-V cache into 'K-V cache' vs 'KV cache' so watch for small naming diffs in the docs.
[12:53] Sara Lin: Anything else from the Redwood team?
[12:57] Matt Gonzalez: I'll summarise next steps after the call and loop in Solutions Engineering and our security team.
[13:04] Jenna Park: One last ask — can we get a whitepaper or short note on your quantization and kernel selection approach? We want to review how it impacts quality.
[13:14] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll attach a short whitepaper and a few benchmark examples comparing different quantization profiles.
[13:22] Matt Gonzalez: Great. Let's recap.
[13:25] (Recap) Matt Gonzalez: Action items: Matt send security packet (SOC2/ISO), Priya share benchmark scripts and runbook, Oliver provision VPC test and creds, Jenna confirm KMS requirements. Schedule: proposed 6-week pilot with the 72-hour benchmark in week 3/4. Acceptance: SOC docs, SSO test, RBAC matrix, audit logs to Splunk, 72-hour benchmark pass.
[13:55] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good. We'll review the packet promptly.
[14:01] Sara Lin: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the packet.
[14:05] Matt Gonzalez: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the email and calendar invites.

End of recording.
